AWARD 


The present reference has been made by the Central Government by its order No. L-300/2/203 dated 2/04/203 
passed in exercise of the powers conferred by clause(d) of sub-section (]) and sub-section(2A) of Section l0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947(/4 of 947) the Central Government hereby refers the said dispute for adjudication. 


“Whether the action of the Management of ONGC, Nhava, in denying the demand of the 
workman Shri Sushil Narayan Khedekar that he be absorbed/given permanency of ONGC 
on the ground of the contract being sham and bogus, is legal and justified? If not, what 
relief the workman is entitled to?” 


The workman has filed his statement of claim. However, despite several opportunities granted by this Tribunal, the 
claimant/workman has failed to file any evidence by way of affidavit or to lead any oral or documentary evidence in 
support of the averments made in the statement of claim. 


The management has remained absent and has not filed any written statement despite repeated opportunities. 


It is not in dispute that the workman has filed his statement of claim. However, mere filing of pleadings is not 
sufficient to establish the allegations made therein. The workman, upon whom the initial burden of proof squarely 
lies, was required to substantiate his claim by leading cogent evidence. 


In the present case, no evidence—oral or documentary—has been led by the workman to prove that the contract was 
sham and bogus or that he was entitled to absorption/permanency. In view of the settled legal position laid down in V. 
K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court, Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court (7), 
and District Administrative Committee v. Secretary-cum-G.M., District Co-operative Bank Ltd., the failure of the 
workman to lead evidence is fatal to the reference. 


In the absence of any evidence in support of the statement of claim, the reference cannot be answered in favour of the 
workman. Consequently, the management is not required to lead any evidence. 


For the foregoing reasons, the reference is answered against the workman. The workman is not entitled to any relief. 
Accordingly, the reference stands answered in terms aforesaid. 
Award as above. 


Justice ARVIND KUMAR MISHRA, Presiding Officer

“Whether Shri Mukesh Rai designated as ‘Supervisor’ under the management of M/s. Nimantran Snacks, Canteen

2. The case is called out today. Both parties are absent on repeated calls. From perusal of record, it is apparent

l. On receiving Order No. L-2604/4/209-IR(M) dated 28.05.2020 from the Government of India, Ministry

2; Mr. Haradhan Sain, General Secretary of Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited Employees’ Union (CITU & 5४४), 
Durgapur Unit filed written statement on 3.0l.2023. Brief fact of petitioner’s case as disclosed in the written 


statement is 


that twenty-two (22) superannuated employees of Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited (hereinafter referred to as FSNL) have 
not been paid Leave Salary and forty-three (43) superannuated employees have not been paid House Rent Allowance 
(hereinafter referred to as HRA) in accordance with to the Memorandum of Settlement dated |.02.20. It is the case 
of the concerned union that the wage revision was granted to the employees who were on the rolls of the company on 
3.2.2006 and they are entitled to HRA as per letter dated 25.07.20I6 and Leave Salary according to the 
Memorandum of Settlement dated .02.20ll. The retired employees entitled to such dues, requested the 
management of FSNL vide letter No. FSNLEU/4I/8 dated 2.07.20l8 for payment. The management neither paid 
any amount nor responded to the representation made through the union. An Industrial Dispute was raised before the 
Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), Raniganj at Durgapur claiming HRA and Leave Salary. The conciliation 
proceeding resulted in a failure and a Failure of Conciliation Report was sent to the Ministry. The appropriate 


government thereafter referred the Industrial Dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication. 


3. Regarding non-payment of Leave Salary, the union pointed out that the Tripartite Wage Agreement was 
signed on |.02.20I], disclosing that it would be effective from 0.0!.2007 to 3.2.20l] and employees including 
those who retired prior to implementation of the agreement but covered under it were paid their regular wage arrears, 
but the management deprived the retired employees of their difference of Leave Salary, consequent upon wage 
revision. Since the wage revision was pending at the time of their retirement, they were paid Leave Salary in respect 
of Earned Leave (EL) and Half Pay Leave (HPL) lying in their credit on the basis of their pre-revised wages. It is 
urged that on revision of wages twenty-two (22) ex-employees, whose list is enclosed, are entitled to difference of 
Leave Salary. The union further contended that management of FSNL made a revision of HRA at the rate of twenty 


percent (20%) of revised Basic Pay from earlier rate 


of ten percent (!0%) with retrospective effect from 0!.04.200 instead of 0.09.20i. The said rule was implemented 
in the month of July / August, 20I5. It is claimed that the consequential arrear dues as per revision should be paid to 
the superannuated employees and they are entitled to revised rate of HRA from 0.04.200 till their retirement. 
Accordingly, union has prayed for payment of the aforesaid dues to the superannuated employees with interest 


thereon from the date it remained unpaid. 


4. Management contested the case by filing written statement on 3.03.2023 through Mr. Saurabh Radhesham 
Tharewal, constituted attorney. According to the management of FSNL the Industrial Dispute is not maintainable in 
its present form. The dispute is vague and indefinite and not sustainable. The main objection raised by the 
management is that there is no provision in the wage agreement dated .02.20l for payment of HRA or Leave 


Salary to the superannuated employees. Referring to Clause No. 4..3 of the agreement it is averred that merely due to

enhancement of Basic Pay on wage revision the employees shall not be entitled to difference of other facilities based

from 0.0.202 to 3.2.20i6 has come into force and the earlier Wage Agreement has lost its force. It is claimed 


that the Industrial Dispute raised is not tenable and is hopelessly barred by limitation. 


5. The central point for consideration is whether the superannuated employees of FSNL are entitled to arrears 
of Leave Salary and HRA as claimed by the union in their letter dated 2.0.209 and whether non-payment of such 


benefits by management is legal and justified. 


6. The union has examined Mr. Haradhan Sain, union representative as Workman Witness No. |. In his 


affidavit-in-chief he reiterated the claim of the 


superannuated employees for payment of difference of Leave Salary on the basis of Wage Agreement signed on 
.02.20I] for the period from 0.0.2007 to 3i.2.20 and for payment of difference of HRA at the revised rate of 
twenty percent (20%) which has been given retrospective effect from 0.04.200. It is stated that there are twenty-two 
(22) retired employees who have prayed for difference of Leave Salary and forty-three (43) employees prayed for 
payment of difference of HRA from 0.04.20i0. The workman witness produced the following documents in support 
of union’s case : 
(i) Copy of representation dated 2.07.208 submitted by the witness as General Secretary, addressed 
to the Unit Head of Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited for payment of arrears of House Rent and Leave 
Salary, is produced as Exhibit ४४-।. 
(ii) Copy of Memorandum of Settlement dated !.02.I, as Exhibit W-2. 
(iii) Copy of the Memorandum of Settlement along with the Terms of Settlement, as Exhibit ४४-२/. 
(iv) Copy of a list of twenty-two retired employees who claimed arrear of Leave Salary and Gratuity, as 
Exhibit W-3. 
(v) Copy of Inter-Office Memo dated 2.07.20I5 by which it was decided that House Rent Allowance 
would be paid at enhanced / revised rate w.e.f. 0.04.200, as Exhibit W-4. 
(vi) Copy of a list of forty-three employees who have not received the revised House Rent Allowance 
w.e.f. 0.04.200 till the date of retirement, as Exhibit W-5. 
(vii) Copy of the Authorization Letter for representing the case of employees, as Exhibit W-6. 
(viii) Copy of Inter-Office Memo dated 25.07.206 for payment of House Rent Allowance, as Exhibit W- 
7 and W-9. 
(ix) Copy of letter dated 2.0!.20I9 addressed to the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), Raniganj at 
Durgapur regarding non-payment of Leave Salary and HRA, as Exhibit W-8. 
(x) Copy of letter dated 30.05.994 issued by the Dy. Manager (P&A), FSNL addressed to the General 
Secretary of FSNL Employees’ Union, regarding recognition of the union, as Exhibit W-0. 


7. Witness denied the suggestion that their union is not a recognized trade union under the Trade Union Act and 
that forty-three (43) listed petitioners were not members of FSNL Employees’ Union during their service period. The 
witness denied that the names of the employees in Enclosure-5 of the written statement were not the members of his 
union or that they have not authorized him to represent their case. During re-cross-examination on 9.02.2025 a 


suggestion was made to the witness that HRA was to be paid from 0.04.20i0 as per Memorandum of Settlement and

the witness admitted the same. The evidence of Workman Witness No. | reveals that the witness is one of the 
signatories of the Memorandum of Settlement dated .02.20. Therefore, it is amply clear that FSNL Employees’ 


Union, Durgapur was a registered and recognized trade union at the relevant time. 


8. No evidence has been adduced by the management of FSNL. The case was fixed up for hearing of argument 


during the Special Campaign. 


9. Mr. Asit Kumar Kolay, learned advocate for the union argued that the superannuated employees whose 
names have been disclosed in Enclosure-3 of the written statement have retired from their service between 30.0.2006 
and 6.02.20l before implementation of the Wage Agreement dated !.02.20l which was applicable to them from 
0I.0.2007 to 3.2.20l and that they are entitled to difference of Leave Salary on the basis of revised pay. It is 
submitted that out of twenty-two (22) employees namely B. Hembrom, S. K. Chakrabarty, Ratan Gope, D. D. Bouri

have been enlisted in

0. Learned advocate for the management in reply contended that the names of the employees are not mentioned 
in the Schedule and it is argued that the employees who have superannuated are not entitled to the benefit of 


difference of HRA and Leave Salary on the basis of the Wage Agreement. 


ll. I have considered the arguments advanced on behalf of the union and management, pleadings of the parties 
and evidence adduced. The list of twenty-two (22) employees claiming payment difference of Leave Salary from 
0I.0.2007 on the basis of revision of pay has been marked as Exhibit W-3 and the list of forty-three (43) retired 
employees, claiming payment of difference of HRA from 0!.04.20I0 is marked as Exhibit W-5. Management of 
FSNL had sufficient notice regarding the identities of the employees but no question was posed to the workman 
witness challenging the identity of any of the employees whose names are mentioned in Exhibits W-3 and W-5. The 
Memorandum of Settlement arrived at between the management of FSNL, Durgapur and their workmen represented 
by FSNL Employees’ Union, Durgapur on |!.02.20l] has been marked as Exhibit W-2/] collectively. On a perusal 
of terms of settlement in Clause No. 2.2. which relates to HRA it is mentioned that the employees covered by the 
Agreement, who are not allotted Company’s quarter, shall be paid house rent allowance equal to the HRA rates as per 
city classification and applicable rates under Government guidelines which is twenty percent (20%) of HRA 
applicable to the cities classified as “Y” to the employees of FSNL and it is further stated that the payment of HRA on 
the basis of revised Basic Pay will be made from 0.04.20i0. Therefore, as per the Memorandum of Settlement the 
employees who were on the payroll of the employer company on 0!.04.200 are entitled to the difference of HRA 


from 0.04.200 till their date of death or superannuation according to the settled rate of enhanced HRA. 


2. The second relief claimed in this case is the payment of difference of Leave Salary to the superannuated 
employees on the basis of Wage Agreement signed on !.02.20ll. Admittedly, there has been a wage revision of the 
employees of FSNL which stood due from 0.0!.2007 on expiry of the previous wage agreement on 3.2.2006. 
According to the Memorandum of Settlement (Exhibit W-2/), the agreement is valid for a period of five years from 


0.0.2007 and it remained operational till 3.2.20. It is undisputed that the employees who were on the payroll of

the company from 0!.0!.2007 till 3.2.20l] are entitled to the revised wages in terms of wage and allowance 
benefits. Clause No. 2..2 provides that the revised wage structure would apply from 0!.0!.2007 for different 
categories of employees as per Annexure-B. This statement suggests that employees who were in service from 
0.0.2007 are entitled to revised pay. Clause No. 4.0 of the Memorandum of Settlement deals with implementation 
of the agreement. It has been agreed upon that the revised wage structure shall come into effect from 0.0.2007 and 
shall continue to be in operation till 3!.2.20I] and in respect of the other provisions, the date of effect would be the 
dates indicated in the respective clauses of the agreement. Payment of Leave Salary is made on the basis of the Basic 
Pay and Dearness Allowance for a period of three hundred days (300) days of outstanding leave at the time of 
superannuation of the employee. If the Basic Pay is revised on 0I.0.2007, the consequential benefit arises in Leave 
Salary would accrue to the employees, commensurate with their outstanding leave. Therefore, the superannuated 
employees, including who have died in harness after 0.0].2007 are entitled to difference of their Leave Salary on the 
basis of revision of wages. Mr. S. K. Banerjee, appearing in the list marked as Exhibit W-3 retired on 30.0.2006 
before the wage agreement came into effect from 0.0.2007. Therefore, he will not be entitled to the payment of 
difference of Leave Salary. Management in their written statement has stated that in Clause No. 4.!.3 of the 
Memorandum of Settlement it is mentioned that merely due to enhancement of Basic Pay, entitlement of the 


employee for different facilities shall 


not change and their eligibility shall remain same. The terms of agreement have stated that the HRA would be 
enhanced by a certain percentage of the Basic Pay and the same would be payable from 0.04.20l0. Therefore, 
management cannot deny its responsibility of paying HRA at an enhanced rate to its forty-three (43) ex-employees. 
Regarding, payment of difference of Leave Salary, management has referred to Clause 4..3 of the agreement and 
argued that entitlement of the employees for other facilities shall not change due to enhancement of Basic Pay and 
their eligibility shall remain same. In order to meet this argument, it is necessary to refer to the provision of Clause 
4..2 of the Memorandum of Settlement where it is stated that the benefits provided for under the previous agreement 
will continue, until otherwise specified in this agreement. The Wage Agreement which came into force from 
0.0.2007 does not contain any provision to curtail the benefit of Leave Salary granted to the employees at the time 
of their retirement. Leave Salary is calculated on the basis of the Basic Pay and Dearness Allowance prevalent at the 
time of superannuation of the employee. The twenty-one (2) of enlisted employees except Mr. S. K. Banerjee would 


therefore be entitled to difference of Leave Salary on the basis of revised pay. 


3. Management in their written statement has contended that another Wage Agreement between management 
and representative of the union has been reached for the period from 0.0.202 to 3.2.206. Therefore, the earlier 
Wage Agreement has lost its force. This argument is devoid of any force as the previous Wage Agreement is applies 
to the employees who were on the payroll of the employer company at the relevant time and their entitlement arises

company did not make payment of difference of HRA and Leave Salary to its retired employees on the basis of 
revision of pay effected from 0!.0.2007, they are certainly entitled to receive such benefits. Their rights would not 


be affected or prejudiced due to a subsequent wage revision applicable 


from 0I.0i.202 to 3.2.20I6, which is not applicable to the enlisted ex-employees herein. It would be just and 


appropriate to direct the management of the employer company to assess the dues of the concerned workmen and

ORDERED 

that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited,

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (9) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-3002/0/2022-IR(M) dated 2.0!.2023 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the employer 
i.e., (L) M/s. Tapas Kumar Chanda Security Agency and (2) Indian Oil Corporation (Pipeline), PHBPL, Bolpur and 


their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“ Whether action of the management of M/s Tapas Kumar Chanda Security Agency terminating the services 
of Sri Swapan Sarkar and not reinstating him in duty, as raised by him vide letter dated 37./2,2029 is proper, legal 


and justified? If not, what relief the disputant is entitled to and what direction, if any, is necessary in the matter? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-3002/0/2022-IR(M) dated 2.0.2023 from the Government of India, Ministry 
of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the Industrial Dispute, a Reference case was registered on 20.0!.2023 and 
an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 


written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. The aggrieved workman initially appeared through Ms. Saswati Thakur, learned advocate and filed his 
written statement on 30.05.2023. The narratives which unfold from the written statement is that the workman is 


an ex-army 


personnel and he joined his service as a private Security Guard in the premises of Indian Oil Corporation Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as IOCL) the Principal Employer through various contractor firms from time to time. The 
workman discharged his work efficiently and received his salary from the Principal Employer. On 09.!2.2020 when 
the workman was preforming his duty at the Colony Main Gate of IOCL (Pipeline) at Bolpur a group of five (5) 
Eunuchs wanted to enter the Colony and he stop them as a security measure and asked them to obtain necessary 
permission from higher authority. They informed that there was a new born baby in the home of Mr. Suniti Tudu, 
Security Officer and they wanted to enter the colony. The petitioner workman made a telephone call to Mr. Tudu and 
informed the incident and also informed the matter to Mr. Ajay Pahuja, DGM but they remain silent and thereafter the 
group of Eunuch assaulted the petitioner and entered the Colony forcibly. The workman checked the Identity Cards of 
the Eunuchs and hand it over to the Mr. Suniti Tudu, Security Officer. After the Eunuchs left the premises. Mr. Suniti 
Tudu, Security Officer of IOCL made a complaint against the petitioner workman before the Office In-charge of the 


Police Station in connection with the incident which occurred on that date. The contractor firm thereafter terminated 


[भाग ॥---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई 4, 2026/ आषाढ 3, 948 6655 


him from service without giving any opportunity. Several appeals were made by the petitioner before the Principal 
Employer but the contractor and the Principal Employer did not pay any heed to his appeals. Petitioner being 
aggrieved with such termination of service without any notice, initiated an Industrial Dispute before the Assistant 
Labour Commissioner (C), Durgapur. The conciliation failed and the matter has been referred to this Tribunal for 
adjudication. It has been prayed that the Opposite Party employers be directed to reinstate the workman with full back 


wages. 


3: Mr. Tapas Kumar Chanda, the proprietor of the Contractor Firm, M/s. Tapas Kumar Chanda Security 
Agency (hereinafter referred to as M/s. TKCSA) (Opposite Party) filed written statement on 26.09.2023. It is 


contended that the 


allegations made in the written statement filed by the petitioner are false. He has not disclosed the actual reason for 
his discontinuation from service under the Principal Employer. It is the case of the contractor firm that Swapan Sarkar 
was engaged as a Security Guard under M/s. Rakesh Kumar Jha Security Agency, having its Office at 26, S.N. 
Banerjee Street, Badrakali, PS- Uttarpara till 30.09.2020. After termination of the contract, Rakesh Kumar Jha left 
IOCL premises without taking any responsibility of continuation of service of the petitioner employed under him due 
to over age and when M/s. TKCSA was entrusted with the contract to provide security service as per terms and 
conditions in the agreement dated 0!.0.2020 and the workman disregarding the terms of agreement, regarding not 
engaging security personnel above sixty (60) years, forcibly occupied the post in the premises of the Principal 
Employer with the help of the local political party. As per work order there was a requirement of thirteen (3) 
Security Guards at the premises of IOCL. The contractor security agency did not have the option to engage any 
person of their choice under political pressure. Opposite Party did not get any opportunity to verify the documents of 
the staff prior to their recruitment. After scrutiny of the documents, the Principal Employer informed that the 
petitioner has already crossed the age limit as per Clause 2.3.7 (page 24) of the Service Agreement and accordingly by 
letter dated 05.0.2020 the Principal Employer requested the proprietor of M/s. TKCSA to provide Security Guards as 
per requirement. The petitioner was discontinued for being over-age and the matter was communicated to him 
accordingly. He was given one month’s time for settling at any other place but he refused to handover his charge to 
the replaced guard and he tried to occupy his post without paying any heed to the request of Principal Employer or the 
Security Agency. Ultimately with the help of Police, Principal Employer replaced the petitioner. The Opposite party 
is an ex-serviceman and has an empanelled Security Agency under the Director General of Resettlement (hereinafter 


referred to as DGR), under the Ministry of Defence. The scheme was introduced to resettle the ex-serviceman 


under Public Sector Undertaking, who retired from their service before the date of his superannuation. An 
Empanelment Certificate in favour of Opposite Party was issued which was valid up to 02.08.202l. The License / 
Empanelment Certificate issued in favour of M/s. TKCSA expired w.e.f. 03.08.202! and the business was closed 
down by the proprietor. As per DGR guidelines Security Agencies would remove the ex-serviceman from the active 
panel of DGR when he attained the age of sixty (60) years and the validity of his empanelment had ceased. However, 
the contract will be allowed to run to completion. The petitioner being a registered member of DGR has ample scope 
for better carrier opportunity in any other agency or organization as per DGR guidelines. Further contention is that on 
0.0.2020 as per Work Order No. 2659368 dated 30.09.2020 all staff engaged under previous agency switch over 
to the Opposite Party by dint of preferential right of their earlier engagement under erstwhile contractor within the 


premises of the Principal Employer. All erstwhile security staff remained engaged at their respective place and 


6656 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 4, 2026/ ASHADHA 3, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


continued their service. The established condition is that contractors will change but the Security Guards would 
continue. The specific case of the contractor firm is that the petitioner has completed sixty (60) years at the time of 
reporting for his duty on 0.0.2020. He had crossed the maximum age for his employment. Accordingly, the 
petitioner had not approached the Tribunal with clean hands. He has made misleading statements and his application 


for reinstatement is liable to be dismissed. 


4. IOCL filed their written statement on 20.li.2023. The specific case of the Principal Employer is that the 
petitioner is an employee under M/s. TKCSA and the Principal Employer has executed a work order bearing No. 
2659368 dated 30.09.2020 for the period from 0.0.2020 to 30.09.2022, as per terms and conditions of the contract. 


It is urged that the application is liable to be dismissed. 
5. Swapan Sarkar examined himself as Workman Witness No. |. He filed his 


affidavit-in-chief stating that he has been working as a private security guard through a contractor firm. He has 
reiterated the statements made in his written statement and claimed that he has been discontinued from his 
employment in a wrongful manner. In his examination-in-chief he produced the following documents : 
(i) Copy of Appointment Letter issued by the Security Agency is produced as Exhibit ४-. 
(ii) Copy of letter dated 0.!2.2020 by which the Security Agency gave Swapan Sarkar prior Notice of 
termination, as Exhibit W-2. 
(iii) Copy of letter dated .2.2020 of Swapan Sarkar addressed to the DGM, IOCL (PHBPL), Bolpur 
sent under registered post, as Exhibit W-3. 
(iv) Copy of a letter dated .2.2020 addressed to Tapas Kumar Chandra Security Agency sent under 
registered post, as Exhibit W-4. 
(५) Copy of application dated 0.02.202] of Swapan Sarkar addressed to the Assistant Labour 
Commissioner (C), Durgapur for saving his job (copy of application is marked as Exhibit W-5). 
(vi) Copy of application dated 02.03.202l of Swapan Sarkar addressed to the Assistant Labour 


Commissioner (C), Durgapur, relating to his termination, as Exhibit W-6. 


6. None appeared for M/s. TKCSA to cross-examine the witness. During cross-examination by IOCL, Principal 
Employer, the witness deposed that he was never appointed by IOCL as a Security Guard and he served IOCL under 
control and supervision of the M/s. TKCSA and produced copy of the Identity Card which has been marked as 
Exhibit W-7. Witness further deposed that he used to receive salary from M/s. TKCSA through bank payment. The 
petitioner stated that he has no grievance against IOCL and he has sought relief against M/s. TKCSA. 

7. No evidence has been adduced by M/s. TKCSA or by IOCL. 


8. The short question for consideration is as to whether the termination of Swapan Sarkar by M/s. TKCSA is 


legal and to what relief the workman is entitled to. 


9. The workman appearing in person and argued that he had been wrongfully terminated from his service by the 
private Security Agency in an illegal manner without issuing any Notice of termination. It is further stated that the 


Security Guard deployed at the premises of IOCL at Bolpur work up to the age of sixty-five (65) years but in his case, 


[भाग II-—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई 4, 2026/ आषाढ 3, 948 6657 


he was illegally discontinued. None appeared for M/s. TKCSA, the contractor firm, which has engaged the workman, 


maintaining the continuity of his service. 


0. Mr. Pradip Kumar Goswami, learned advocate for the management of IOCL argued that the petitioner 
workman has no employer-employee relationship with IOCL. The workman was never appointed by IOCL and in his 
cross-examination the WW-I admitted such fact. The witness also stated that he has not prayed for any relief against 


IOCL. 


ll. I have considered the argument advanced by the petitioner and learned advocate for IOCL in light of the 
pleadings and evidence on record. It may be gathered from the written statement of M/s. TKCSA that Swapan Sarkar 
was engaged as a Security Guard under M/s. Rakesh Kumar Jha Security Agency till 30.09.2020. According to the 
Work Order No. 2659368 dated 30.09.2020, the Principal Employer engaged M/s. TKCSA to provide private 
Security Guards to IOCL, Bolpur from 0.0.2020. The Principal Employer in Paragraph No. 2 of their written 
statement stated that the Work Order was issued in favour of M/s. TKCSA from 0I.l0.2020 to 30.09.2022. 


According to the Private Security Agency the 


petitioner ex-serviceman had attained sixty (60) years of age and as per terms and conditions of the contract the 
service of Swapan Sarkar could not be continued. The Opposite Party, Security Agency did not produce the copy of 
the contract to prove that the petitioner had attained sixty years of age or for such reason he was not entitled to be 
continued as a Security Guard from 0I.!0.2020. No attempt was made on the part of Security Agency to prove that 
the proper Notice of termination was issued to him disclosing the reason of termination. From Exhibit १४-।, the Letter 
of appointment of Swapan Sarkar issued by M/s. TKCSA, I find that the date of birth of Swapan Sarkar is 05.0.96l. 
Therefore, the workman did not complete sixty years of age on 0I.0.2020. It is true that a letter dated 0.2.2020 
(Exhibit W-2) was issued by the Security Agency to Swapan Sarkar and in the said letter, the termination of service 
was given effect from the very next dated i.e., !].!2.2020. Though the service of the workman was contractual in 
nature but from the material on record and the admission of the contractor firm I find that the contract between the 
employer and contractor firm is formal and in Paragraph No. 7 of the written statement that the Opposite Party had no 
scope to engage a single person of his choice due to political pressure and they were under compulsion to appoint the 
same Security Guards who were working under previous contractor. Under such situation the aggrieved workman is 
entitled to a clear one month’s notice before his termination, in default he is entitled to be paid one month’s wage 
from the period of Notice and as per provision under Section 25-F of the I.D. Act, 947 the workman would be 
entitled to retrenchment compensation on the basis of continuous service rendered. In the present case the petitioner 
workman failed to establish how many years of continuous service he has rendered and whether he has continuously 
worked for 240 days in the preceding twelve months. I therefore hold that in the present case the only relief the 
petitioner workman would get is Pay for one month in lieu of Notice of termination. Since the workman was not 


appointed by the Principal Employer and he has claimed no relief against the Principal Employer, he is 


therefore not entitled to reinstatement in the service of Security Guard under IOCL. For abrupt termination of 
workman without Notice of termination much earlier to his attaining sixty (60) years of age on 04.0.202, it would 
be just and appropriate to grant a one-time compensation of Rs.,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) to the workman, 


payable by M/s. TKCSA along with one (l) month’s Pay in lieu of Notice prior to his termination. 


6658 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 4, 2026/ ASHADHA 3, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Hence, 
ORDERED 
that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest against Indian Oil Corporation (Pipeline), PHBPL, Bolpur, 
Principal Employer. It is allowed ex-parte in part against M/s. Tapas Kumar Chanda Security Agency. The Private 
Security Agency having terminated the workman without prior Notice of one month shall be liable to pay one (J) 
month’s Pay to the workman Swapan Sarkar along with a one-time compensation of 75५.] ,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh 
only) for abrupt termination of his work. The Security Agency shall pay the said amounts within two (2) months from 
the date of communication of the Award. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the 
Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour and Employment , Government of India, New Delhi for 


information and Notification.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub —section (2A) of Section l0 of 
the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947) Government Of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No.L-2002/74/2009-IR(CM-I) dated 04/2/2009 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer i.e. management of M/s. Tata Steel Ltd., Jamadoba, Dhanbad and their workman through the Member, 
Rashtriya Colliery MazdoorSangh, Dhanbad for adjudication by this Tribunal: 


SCHEDULE 


“i) Whether the action of the Management of Tata Steel Limited, in not providing dependant 
employment to Sri Purushotam Kumar, son of Late Kapildeo Mandal, Belt Operator is justified and legal?” ii) 
To what relief is the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal entitled?” 


2. The case of the workman as per the written statement filed on his behalf is that Late Kapildeo Mandal having 
P.No. 26655 was employed as Belt Operator in No. 6 and 7 Pits of Jamadoba Colliery of M/s. Tata Steel Ltd. and he 
was continuously employed putting in unblemished record of service from 26.07.984 to 30.03.2006 and after 22 
years of this service after doing his shift duty on 30.03.2006 from 5:00 P.M. to :00 A.M. he deposited his Cap Lamp 
in Lamp Cabin and while he was leaving from his place of work, he was killed on the way in the premises of the Tata 
Steel Ltd. at distance of about !00 Meters to the work place but after his death his dependent son was not given 
employment in lieu of his father Late Kapildeo Mandal disregarding innumerable requests of his family members and 
of the union and therefore Industrial Dispute was raised which ended in failure in conciliation resulting the reference 
of his case before this Tribunal. As the accident of killing took place in the premises of the company so his dependent 
was entitled for employment in all bonafides but it was denied to him by the company although in such nature of case 


6666 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 4, 2026/ ASHADHA 3, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


the company has given dependent employment in several cases which is discriminatory, improper, unfair and illegal 
and at last it was prayed to direct the company for providing dependent employment of the deceased employee. 


3. On the other hand the case of the management as per the written statement filed on his behalf is that the 
present reference is not maintainable. The employees of Jharia Division of Tata Steel Ltd. are guided by the bipartite 
agreement with the union in respect of dependent employment. As per the employment procedure of the company 
employment will be offered to the male dependent of an employee who meets with fatal accident or suffers permanent 
total disability (l00%) due to an accident while on duty. In the absence of an adult male dependent, employment may 
be offered to the widow and the widow so employed may, if she so wishes, resign from services in favour of 
employment of her son on his attaining majority. The benefit under employees family benefit scheme may be 
extended to the family in lieu of employment if so opted. This will be in addition to the accident compensation 
payable in such cases. According to the employment procedure of the company in vogue the son of Late Kapildeo 
Mandal is not entitled for employment in the Steel Company. The deceased employee was appointed on 26.07.984 
and expired on 3!.03.2006. He was an underground employee at 6&7 Pits Colliery. The underground employee is 
required to get his attendance booked in ‘C’ form register in the attendance cabin at the beginning of the shift and get 
himself ‘OUT’ before leaving the colliery premises at the end of the shift. An underground employee is also required 
to take the cap lamp from the lamp cabin situated at the pit top before going underground and deposit the same at the 
lamp cabin at the end of the shift before leaving the colliery premises. On 30.03.2006, the deceased employee was in 
‘B’ shift duty commencing from 5:00 P.M. on 30.03.2006 to :00 A.M. of 3.03.2006 at 6&7 Pits Colliery and was 
deployed to work as Belt Operator in the colliery. Accordingly he got his attendance booked in Form ‘C’ Register at 
the attendance cabin in the beginning of the shift and also got him ‘OUT?’ at the end of the shift. He had deposited his 
cap lamp in the cap lamp cabin of 6&7 Pits Colliery at the end of the shift before leaving the colliery premises. He 
had neither met with any accident nor received any injury while on duty in ‘B’ Shift i.e. from 5:00 PM on 30.03.2006 
to :00 A.M. on 3.03.2006. Usha Devi wife of Late Kapildeo Mandal filed a case under Workmen’s Compensation 
Act for payment of compensation before the Workmen’s Compensation Commissioner, Dhanbad who referred the 
same to the P.O Labour Court, Dhanbad for adjudication that was registered as WC Case No. 4/2009 and after hearing 
the parties the Ld. Court held that the deceased employee has not received any injury in course of employment and so 
the applicant is not entitled for compensation and in view of this matter the son of deceased employee was not entitled 
for employment as per provision of employment procedure of the company. In rejoinder portion the management has 
also taken the same stand and denied the entitlement of the applicant and at last it was prayed to hold that the son of 
Late Kapildeo Mandal is not entitled for any relief in this case. 


4. The workman has also submitted his rejoinder to the W/S filed on behalf of the management submitting that 
the dependent employment is an automatic condition and if an employee dies during the service tenure as per NCWA 
his dependent is entitled to the service. The workman has denied all the stands taken by the management in its written 
statement. 


5. Issue 
On the basis of pleadings of both the parties following issue has been framed: 


“?) Whether the action of the Management of Tata Steel Limited, in not providing dependant employment to 
Sri Purushotam Kumar, son of Late Kapildeo Mandal, Belt Operator is justified and legal? And if not, to what relief 
is the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal entitled?” 


6. To prove his case the applicant Purushotam Kumar has examined himself as WW-I. 
7 No documentary evidence has been adduced from the side of the workman. 

8. On the other hand the management has examined ॥५४-] Sapan Kumar Patra.

40. Heard both sides and perused the materials on record. 


Il. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the workman has submitted that Late Kapildeo Mandal was permanent 
employee of Tata Steel Ltd. and he commenced his duty from 5 P.M. on 30.03.2006 to | A.M. on 3.03.2006 and 
after completing his duty he was returning to his home but unfortunately he was killed at a distance of about l00 
meters from his work place. He had rendered continuous service of 22 years since 26.07.984 to 3.03.2006. He died 
during tenure of his service so his dependent son Purushotam Kumar is entitled to employment in his place as per 
NCWA but his claim was rejected by the management on the ground that the provision of NCWA are not applicable 
in his case. He had filed W.C. Case No. 0/2009 that was rejected by the P.O. Labour Court, Dhanbad holding that he 
was not killed in course of employment and against that order he has preferred M.A. No. 293 of 200 before the 
Hon’ble Jharkhand High Court. His claim is not based only on the ground of death of his father during course of 
employment but also as per the provision of NCWA and in similar situation the management had provided 
employment to the dependent of one Late Geeta Devi. 


2. On the other hand the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the management has submitted that as per the employment 
procedure of the company the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal is not entitled for employment in the Steel Company 
because as per the employment procedure the dependent of an employee is entitled for employment in case an 
employee meets with fatal accident or suffers permanent total disability due to an accident while on duty but the same 
is not applicable in case of the present reference. The applicant had also filed W.C. Case No. /2009 but the same was 
rejected by the Labour Court, Dhanbad and this reference case has no merit and so prayed to dismiss the same. 


3. Now as regards the oral evidence adduced in this case from the side of the applicant, ऐैफृ-] Purushotam 
Kumar who is the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal has deposed that Late Kalidas Mandal was permanent employee of 
Tata Steel Ltd. and on 30.03.2006 and he commenced his duty from 5 P.M. on 30.03.2006 to | A.M. on 3].03.2006 
and after completing his duty he was returning to his home but unfortunately he was killed at a distance of about l00 
meters from his work place. He had rendered continuous service of 22 years since 26.07.984 to 3.03.2006. He died 
during tenure of his service and so his dependent son Purushotam Kumar is entitled to employment in his place as per 
NCWA but his claim was rejected by the management on the ground that the provision of NCWA are not applicable 
in his case. He filed W.C. Case No. 0/2009 that was rejected by the P.O. Labour Court, Dhanbad holding that he was 
not killed in course of employment and against that order he has preferred M.A. No. 293 of 200 before the Hon’ble 
Jharkhand High Court. His claim is not based only on the ground of death of his father during course of employment 
but also as per the provision of NCWA. In cross-examination he has stated that he filed application for employment in 
place of his father who died due to accident during the tenure of service and he had also filed the case before the 
Workmens’ Compensation Commissioner claiming compensation being W.C. Case No. 0/2009 that was transferred 
to Labour Court, Dhanbad where it was held that as his father had not died due to accident in course of employment, 
he was not entitled to get compensation. He has denied the fact that his father had not died during course of 
employment. He has further stated that he has no knowledge if there is any procedure in Tata Company regarding 
dependent employment or any provision of NCWA and denied the suggestion that he is not entitled to dependent 
employment. 


4. No documentary evidence has been adduced from the side of the applicant in this case. 


5. Now as regards the oral evidence of the management, ५४-। Sapan Kumar Patra who is working as clerk at 
General Manager’s Office Jamadoba of Tata Steel Ltd. has deposed that as per the employment procedure of the 
company, the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal is not entitled for employment in the Steel Company because as per the 
employment procedure the dependent of an employee is entitled for employment in case an employee meets with a 
fatal accident or suffers permanent total disability due to an accident while on duty but the same is not applicable in 
case of the present reference. The applicant had also filed W.C. Case No. !/2009 but the same was rejected by the 
Labour Court, Dhanbad and this reference case has no merit. In cross-examination he has stated that the workman 
died during his service. He cannot say if the dependent gets employment in coal industries after the death of his parent 
employee. He also cannot say if NCWA is applicable in Tata Company. 


6. Now as regards the documentary evidence adduced from the side of the management, Exhibit M-I is the 
copy of order dated 0.0.200 passed by the P.O, Labour Court, Dhanbad in W.C. Case No. 0!/2009 that was filed 
by one Usha Devi, wife of Late Kapildeo Mandal against the Manager of TISCO Colliery claiming compensation of 
Rs. 3,68,340/- for death of her husband in TISCO Colliery but her case was dismissed by the Labour Court holding 
that the deceased workman was not murdered in course of employment. Exhibit M-4 to M-9 are the certified copies 
of deposition of the witnesses namely Purushotam Kumar, Usha Devi, Mohan Turi, Govind Prasad, Raghvendra 
Kumar Nirala and Sapan Kumar Patro respectively in W.C. Case No. 0I/2009 that ultimately resulted in dismissal. 
Exhibit M-2 is copy of procedure for employment of employee-wards at Jharia Group of Collieries dated 27..997 
in which it has been stated that an employee on completion of (5 years of satisfactory service may register one of 
his/her dependents in the approved category (son, brother, adopted son, son-in-law and grandson) for employment on 
his service and employment will be offered, unless otherwise stated, to the registered dependent of an employee who 
ceases to be in employment after completing 30 years or more service, subject to the availability of vacancy in the 
standard force and requirement. Such employment to the registered dependents may be offered along with those in 


6668 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 4, 2026/ ASHADHA 3, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


temporary pool subject to priorities agreed with the union. Employment will be offered to the male dependent of an 
employee who meets with a fatal accident or suffers permanent total disability (l00%) due to an accident while on 
duty. In the absence of an adult male dependent, employment may be offered to the widow and the benefit under 
Employees’ Family Benefit Scheme may be extended to the family in lieu of employment if so opted and this will be 
in addition to the accident compensation payable in such cases. Exhibit M-3 is the copy of Chapter-IX of NCWA-IV 
which deals with the Social Security such as Life Cover Scheme, Workmen’s Compensation Benefits as well as 
Employment to the dependent out of which Rule 9.4. is relevant for this case which says that Employment would be 
provided to one dependent of workers disabled permanently and those who meet with death while in service. 


7. On perusal of Exhibit M-2 it is evident that the case of the applicant does not fall under any of the categories 
mentioned therein but as regards Exhibit M-3 which is copy of Chapter-IX of NCWA-IV and got exhibited on behalf 
of the management in his favour, on careful perusal of Rule 9.4. it is clear that there are 2 categories who have been 
given entitlement to the dependent employment out of which No. | is dependent of workers disabled permanently and 
No.2 is those who meet with death while in service and the case of the present applicant falls in the second category 
as the deceased Kapildeo Mandal died/killed while in service and therefore the present applicant namely Purushotam 
Kumar who is the son of Late Kapildeo Mandal who was permanent Belt Operator in Jharia division of M/s. Tata 
Steel Limited, is entitled to the dependent employment in place of his father who died on 3].03.2006. 


8. MW-I!, Sapan Kumar Patra though has deposed in Paragraph-5 of his examination-in-chief that the 
employment provision of NCWA is not applicable in Tata Steel Limited but in his cross-examination he has stated 
that he cannot say whether NCWA is applicable to Tata Company or not and therefore the evidence of this witness on 
this point does not support the case of management in any way. 


Though in the note of 9.4.] it has been mentioned that in regard to the employment of dependent of 
employees, TISCO will follow their existing practices but it has nowhere categorically been mentioned in it that the 
Rules of the NCWA will not be applicable in case of employment to the dependent of the TISCO employees. 


9. Thus on the basis of above appreciations of the facts, circumstances and evidences on record this Tribunal 
finds and holds that the action of the management of Tata Steel Limited in not providing dependent employment to 
Sri Purushotam Kumar son of Late Kapildeo Mandal, Belt Operator is neither justified nor legal and accordingly he is 
entitled to the dependent employment in place of his father. The issue is decided in favour of the applicant and the 
Management is directed to provide employment to the applicant Purushotam Kumar within a period of 3 months from 
the date of publication of this Award. The reference is answered accordingly. 


Let the copies of Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, 
New Delhi for information and notification.

following relief:- 


To pass an Award holding that order of termination issued by the Respondent/Management dated 3.05.20I7 
terminating the services of the Petitioner from 5.05.207 is illegal, arbitrary and contrary to law and liable to be set 
aside and consequently, direct the Respondents to reinstate the Petitioner into service with full back wages, continuity 
of service and other attendant benefits with costs. 


2. As per the claim statement, the Petitioner is an ex-service man served in Indian Army for |8 years. The 
Employment Exchange sponsored his name to the Respondent for the post of Assistant. The petitioner was selected 
and appointed by an order dated 05.07.997 by the respondent Corporation on consolidated wages of Rs.327.80 for 
the period from 09.07.997 to 06.09.997. The Petitioner though termed to be temporary Assistant, but he had been 
discharging the work of permanent Assistant. The Petitioner was expecting absorption and regularisation of 
service, but the 2" Respondent by an order dated 3.05.20I7 has terminated the services of the Petitioner w.e.f 
5.05.20!7. No reason has been assigned as to why services of the Petitioner has been terminated. While the 
Petitioner has worked for more than 240 days within a period of 2 calendar months prior to termination. 

The Petitioner has rendered the service for about twenty years, the Respondent after paying meager wages 
has failed to absorb the services of the Petitioner. The Petitioner has relied on the case law in LIC Employees 
Association Vs LIC of India (205) 2 LLN |. Hence, the present dispute is raised before this Tribunal. 


3. The Respondent in its reply statement stated that the Petitioner’s service was temporary. He was disengaged 
upon attaining 60 years of age, since there was no scope for employment. The Respondent submits that judgement 
reported in LIC Employees Association Vs LIC of India is not applicable to the Petitioner. The Petitioner was 
appointed under regulation 8 of the LIC . He worked without demur. He chose to take examination but was 
unsuccessful . Hence, the claim of the Petitioner is untenable. He was provided with an opportunity for regular 
absorption by allowing him to take written examination for selection of Assistant on 3.08.2008. But, the Petitioner 
was unable to utilize that opportunity as he did not come out successful in the written examination.

7. The first point that arises for determination is whether the judgement rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 
the cases of Mr. A.V.Nachane Vs Union of India (AIR 982 SC PP i26) and Mr. M.Venugopal vs. Divisional 
Manager LIC, Machilipatnam (AIR [994 SC PP 343) is applicable to the present case on hand and consequently, 
the Petitioner is debarred to raise an industrial dispute? 


8. On perusal of the above mentioned judgements, it appears that judgements do not lay down blanket rule that 
Petitioner is always debarred from raising an Industrial dispute after these two judgements. These two judgements 
recognizes limited solution of right to raise an Industrial Dispute in specific circumstances. In the case of Mr. 
A.V.Nachane Vs Union of India (supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court examined the amendments of LIC of India Act 
which allowed service conditions to be governed by statutory rules overriding the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 
Those rules which were approved by the Hon'ble Supreme Court operates notwithstanding the provisions of Industrial 
Disputes Act, !947. Thus, if the matter is governed by overriding statutory rules, then usually, the industrial dispute 
is barred. But, if the matter is not governed by such rules, then , the industrial dispute is allowable. 


9. Now, I have to examine whether the case of the Petitioner is governed under the amended Rules?. For 
this, I have to ascertain the exact subject of the dispute. The Rules mentioned above in para No.4 do not have 
overriding effect of the provisions of section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, !947, which runs as under:- 


“25F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. 


- No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an 
employer shall be retrenched by that employer until- 


(a) the workman has been given one month 5 notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the period 
of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; 


(b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days 
‘average pay [for every completed year of service] (w.e.f. /9.72./964),] or any part thereof in excess of six months; 
and 


(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government [or such authority as may be specified 
by the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette.” 


0. Thus, section 25F of the Act deals with conditions precedent to retrenchment of workman and mandated 
that employer cannot retrench the workman, unless follow/comply with the mandatory steps provided under 
section 25F, which are as under:- 


i) One month notice (or wages in lieu thereof); 


ii) |Retrenchment compensation i.e, equal to I5 days average pay for every completed year of service or any part 
thereof in excess of six months and this amount must be paid at the time of retrenchment. 


ll. Admittedly, the mandate provided under the section 25F was not followed by the Respondent/Management. 
Hence, the industrial dispute raised by the Petitioner is maintainable. 


2. The second point that arises for determination is whether the Petitioner has worked as workman for more 
than 240 days continuously in a year? 


3. The answer to the question emerges from the documents marked on behalf of the Petitioner. Ex.WI is copy 
of appointment order issued by Respondent/Management to the Petitioner dated 05.07.997. Ex.W2 suggests that 
Petitioner was transferred on 07.04.2008. Ex.W4 is the copy of statement of bank account of the Petitioner reflecting 
monthly salary credited into his account. On perusal of the record, it appears that Petitioner was paid monthly salary 
regularly for several years and his service was terminated by letter dated 3.05.20I7. From the date of entry into 
service, the Petitioner has received salary upto 5.05.20l7 continuously without any interruption. Hence, this fact 
is established that the Petitioner has worked for more than 240 days continuously in a calendar year. 


4. The third point that arises for determination is to what relief the Petitioner is entitled to? 


5. As per discussion above, the Respondent/Management LIC Corporation had failed to comply with the 
mandatory provisions u/s.25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, l947. i.e., No notice was issued to the Petitioner; no 
wages was paid in lieu of notice as well as compensation equal to l5 days average pay for every completed year 
of service or any part thereof in excess of six months. Thus, the retrenchment becomes illegal, void and ab initio. 


It is worth to mention that provisions of section 25F of the Act are mandatory and not only procedural and its 
violation converts into result of reinstatement. But, in the present case on hand, the Petitioner has already attained 
the age of superannuation and therefore, there is no occasion to pass an order of reinstatement. Therefore, instead of 


[भाग [Ive 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई 4, 2026/ आषाढ 3, 948 6677 
reinstatement, it is appropriate to pass an order to pay one month wages in lieu of notice; compensation i.e, equal to 
5 days average pay for every completed year of service or any part thereof in excess of six months. 

AWARD 


In view of the foregoing discussion, the claim petition filed by the Petitioner is liable to be allowed with 
the following directions to the Respondent/Management :- 


i) To pay the Petitioner one month wages in lieu of notice; 


ii) |Retrenchment compensation i.e, equal to 5 days average pay for every completed year of service or any part 
thereof in excess of six months. 


iii) Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) as lumpsum compensation for illegal retrenchment. 


All these above mentioned amounts shall be paid to the Petitioner by the Respondent/Management within a period 
of two months after publication of Award and if the Respondent fails to pay these amounts within the prescribed

As per reference letter dated 04/05/202 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference 
has been made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, !947 (in short the 'Act') as per 
Notification No. L-4302/8/20!l (R(B-M) dt. 04.05.202. The dispute under reference relates to: 


"Whether the action of the management of Steel Authority of India Ltd., in not giving post and scale of pay 
accordance to nature of job and in terminating the services of Shri Prabhu Nath S/o Shri Gaya Prasad w.e-f. 
9.6./997, is legal and justified? What relief the workman is entitled to?" 


Claimant/workman Shri Prabhu Nath (hereinafter stated as the claimant) has filed the statement of claim with 
averments which may be concisely stated as hereunder: 


L. The claimant/worker was appointed to the post of Peon/Messenger in the defendant establishment in the year 
983. 
2: The claimant/worker's work was of a permanent nature, but the employer did not provide him with the salary 


or designation commensurate with the nature of his work. When the plaintiff worker demanded a designation 
and salary scale in accordance with the nature of his work, the employer became displeased and suddenly 
terminated his services on June 9, 997. 


3. The claimant/worker had been continuously employed from 983 to June 8, 997, without an interruption. 


[भाग ॥---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई 4, 2026/ आषाढ 3, 948 668] 


4. 


The employers did not comply with the mandatory provisions of Section 257 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 
947, while terminating the plaintiff worker's services, as the claimant was neither given notice nor severance 
pay, nor any notice pay before the termination of his services. 


The respondent employers, being aggrieved by the award of the Hon'ble Labour Court, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, 
filed Writ Petition No. 3495/200, Steel Authority of India Ltd. vs. State of U.P. and others, in the Hon'ble 
High Court, Allahabad. In its judgment dated February 2!, 20ll, the Hon'ble High Court held that the 
appropriate government in relation to the disputes of Steel Authority of India is the Central Government. 
Therefore, the reference issued by the Hon'ble Labour Court and the award passed thereon by the Hon'ble 
Labour Court No. 3, Kanpur, were accordingly set aside. beyond its jurisdiction and consequently not 
sustainable, and were accordingly set aside. 


Based on the above facts, the termination of the claimant worker's service is unjust and illegal. Therefore, the 
claimant worker is entitled to reinstatement in service with continuity of service and full back wages and other 
admissible benefits for the entire period of unemployment. 


Respondent side has submitted the written statement with averments which may be summarized as stated below: 


l. 


The reasons / recital on the basis of which the Central Government has formed it's opinion of existence of 
Industrial dispute is conspicuously missing in the impugned reference order. The said order is inconsistent to 
the finding of Hon'ble Apex Court in a case between M/s. Swadeshi Cotton Mills and Industrial Tribunal II 
reported in (950-67) S.C.L.J. Page No. 389. 


The Central Government has not applied it's mind diligently in as much that it miserably failed to consider 
the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a case between Secretary State of Karnataka V/s Uma 
Devi and others reported in 2006(09) F.L.R. 826, and subsequently in another case between Union of India 
and others V/s Vartak Labour Union reported in 20l(i29) F.L.R. 500, wherein it has been categorically 
held that daily wagers, casual and contract Labours have no lien in the employment in public sectors. 


Neither the services of applicant have been prop dismissed, retrenched, terminated nor has he been deprived 
from work allegedly from 9.6.997 in any manner whatsoever. 


No cause of action had accrued to the applicant on (b) establishme 9.6.97 nor on any other date in any 
manner whatsoever. 


The applicant had never been appointed with opposite party establishment in any capacity in any manner 
import whatsoever, as such the question of termination of his services does not arise. 


He had never been appointed with Opposite Party in any capacity at any point of time, neither in the year 
983, as alleged. The Opposite Party is a Government of India company, and no post of peon exists in it, as 
alleged. It is pertinent to mention here that recruitment to posts in the company is on the basis of laid down 
procedures and statutory rules after holding requisite tests and interviews. The applicant has never undergone 
any of the recruitment procedures, thus proving that he was never recruited. Had he been recruited, he would 
have been issued appointment letter and his name would have figured in the official records of attendance 
maintained by the Opposite Party establishment. He would also have been issued several other important 
documents such as identity card, pay slip and leave book by the Opposite Party establishment. 


It is reiterated that he had Jo Lever been in the employment of Opposite Party, as such the provisions of Sec. 
25F Industrial Disputes Act 947 are neither attracted, nor is he entitled to benefits there under. It is further 
denied that other individuals even lower in post than the applicant have been working in the establishment of 
Opposite Party, therefore, the provisions of sec 25G of ments of pars !2 which are a matter of the ID Act are 
also not attracted. 


Furthermore, recruitment on regular posts in the company is on the basis of laid down procedure, various 
statutory rules including that of reservation for the posts of SC/ST (OBC and PWD may not have been 
applicable at the relevant time) and after requisite tests and interviews. Successful candidates are issued 
appointment letters for respective posts and given pay scales accordingly, besides their names are enrolled on 
the attendance register, the employees of the opposite party are issued identity cards, pay slips, leave book 
etc. and their salaries are credited in their respective bank accounts. 


Irrespective of regular and permanent work there is casual and intermittent work of loading unloading and 
staking of iron and steel goods in Warehouses of Opposite Party which is entrusted to the handling 
contractors by inviting tenders, and contractors offering lowest bid are allotted the contract of loading 
unloading and staking through a written agreement for a specified period. The handling contractors deploy 
their own contract labours to full fill the contractual obligations and the Opposite Party pays directly to such 
Handling Contractor according to bills raised by him in terms of agreement.

During the trial applicant Prabhu Nath died. 


By way of order dated 4.09.2022 his wife Pushpa Devi is corporated against him and the case is further fixed for 
evidence of the claimant side. 


As per claim statement, claimant requested that he was appointed in 983 as Peon/messenger by O.P. and his nature 
of work is permanent but they were never given to him as per nature, pay and name and suddenly his services was 
terminated on date 09.06.997. He had worked from 983 to 08.06.997 continuous without any break. 


In reply of that opposite party, in our written statement is stated that Applicant has never appointed with opposite 
party establishment in any capacity in any manner whatsoever, as such the question of his services does not arise. 


Further said, in our additional statement in para l8, respective of regular and permanent work there is casual and 
intermittent work of loading and unloading In para 20 stated that applicant Prabhu Nath had been offered in the post 
of complete such emergent casual and intermittent unskilled work arises in exigencies from time to time on initially 
and mutually agreed amount and when he had been available and paid remuneration through contingent fund 
according the bills raised by him for such work. 


Now, the question is whether the applicant is appointed in opposite party organisation for above question the evidence 
of the parties is important. 


The applicant never filled any documentary evidence he had given oral evidence only and examine himself. 


In his chief examination, he supported our claim statement. Chief examination stated that I was employed at the 
respondent establishment as a peon/messenger since 983. Another employee, who worked as a cleaner, was also 
hired in 983. We were both terminated from our jobs on June 9, 997. We were dismissed verbally. Our services 
were terminated by Mr. Sanjeev Saurabh, the Branch Manager, through a verbal order. We had worked continuously 
from 983 to June 6, 997. We received our salaries directly from the company. The company prepared our salary 
slips, and we received our wages through them. In cross examination stated no application was submitted for 
employment with the department. The department hired us without any formal process. We did not receive any 
appointment letter from the department. But I was given a character certificate. We received our salary through salary 
vouchers. I don't know if all employees were paid by check by the establishment, but we were paid in cash. All 
employees signed the attendance register maintained by the defendant establishment, but a separate register was 
maintained for us, which has been submitted to the court. Document number ७/। was given to me by the branch 
manager. Initially, I went to the RLC with this matter, where they said it was a state issue. Then I went to the Labour 
Court in the state. 


In claim statement and rejoinder applicant stated that he had worked from !983 to 08.06.997 without any break but 
he had never given any documentary evidence that proved he had worked for above period. 


As per ID Act section 25 B is read as under:

25-58. Definition of continuous service-For the purposes of this Chapter- (() a workmen shall be said to be 
in continuous service for a period if he is, for that period, in uninterrupted service, including service 
accident or a strike which is not illegal, or a lock-out or a cessation of work which may be interrupted on 
account of sickness or authorised leave of which is not due to any fault on the part of the workman; 


(2) where a workman is not in continuous service within the mean of clause (/)ि a period of one 
year or six months, he shall be deemed be in continuous service under an employer- 


(a) for a period of one year, if the workman, during a period of twel calendar months preceding the 
date with reference to whis calculation is to be made. has actually worked under the employe for 
not less than- 


(i) one hundred and ninety days in the case of a workmar employed below ground in a 
mine; and 


(ii) two hundred and forty days, in any other case; 


It is mandatory that worker has worked 240 days as per provision because applicant has not given any documentary 
evidence and against that opposite party said that he had offered in pass to complete such emergent casual and some 
work not appointed in his oral evidence claimant said as quoted above he never applied for any employment, he kept 
as by department, no any appointment letter has been given, his salary was given by way of vouchers, he paid cash. 


The applicant had been offered in past to complete such emergent casual and intermittent unskilled works arisen on 
exigencies from time to time on initially on mutually agreed amount, as and when he had been available and paid 
remunerations through contingent fund according to bills raised by him for such work. 


After showing of all evidence, it is clear no appointment letter was given to him, he paid cash but he had not given 
any documentary evidence that he had worked as employee in opposite party organisation or he had worked in 
preview of section 25 B. 


In view of the foregoing discussion and in the given circumstance the reference stands disposed of as of ‘Nil’ award.

" Whether the action of the management of Steel Authority of India Ltd., Kanpur/M/s. Onkar enterprises, Noida in

Claimant/workman Shri Ram Sevak (hereinafter stated as the claimant) has filed the statement of claim with 
averments which may be concisely stated as hereunder: 


l. | The applicant was continuously employed as a gunman and security guard from 2009 until the morning of 
December 3], 20l3, under the direction of the employers. However, his services were terminated on the 
evening of December ३], 203, through a verbal order. 


2. The third party was authorized to conduct inspections and confirmations to ensure compliance with the 
directions of the first and second respondents, and the security work was carried out and is still being 
performed. 


3. The applicant was employed informally from September |, 2009, to December 3, 20I3. The third party was 
also appointed through the first and second parties, and this appointment resulted in a violation of the 
petitioner's rights under the Labour Act, 947. The applicant was deprived of his earned wages, including 
overtime pay, which was not paid according to the rules. This was also protested by the petitioner. 


4. It is submitted that the applicant was not paid the amount due to him as per the rules. Two types of documents 
were used for obtaining signatures. If any objection was raised, the employee was dismissed and deprived of his 
service, which constitutes a violation of the rights granted under the Education Act of 947 and 948. This 
persistent and unwavering harassment is unjust and illegal. 


5. 7 is further submitted that the employer/defendant parties did not give the applicant any opportunity to 
complain throughout his entire period of service, nor were any charges levelled against him. Despite this, his 
dismissal and deprivation of service is unjust and illegal. 


6. The service of applicant in this case, which was terminated on 3!-2-203, is unjust and illegal. No notice pay 
or compensation was given. The service was terminated verbally, even though the petitioner is entitled to all 
due payments. 


7. It is requested that an order be passed directing the restoration of service continuity under the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 947, and awarding compensation for the period of unemployment, severance pay, and other 
previously unpaid dues, including bonuses.

authorised leave of which is not due to any fault on the part of the workman;

7. On perusal of the counter statement filed by the Respondent/bank, it is clear that the 
Petitioner has filed the claim petition u/s. 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, [947 before this 
Tribunal belatedly. Admittedly, the Petitioner was discharged from duty by Respondent bank 
w.e.f. 2..208 and the Petitioner has filed the claim petition on 02.09.2022. The learned 
counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent argued that the industrial dispute has been filed 
after the prescribed limitation period and therefore, it is liable to be rejected as not maintainable. 


8. He relied on the case law in Shri Ravikumar Vs. Management of Tamil Nadu Transport 
Corporation , Tirunelveli Division. The facts of the case are as follows:- 


The Petitioner in that case was working as driver with the Respondent Corporation and was 
dismissed from service on 04.04.2005. The Petitioner raised a dispute before the Labour Office 
on 02.0.20I4 in which failure report was given on 25.03.20I4. The Petitioner has raised an 
Industrial Dispute No.64/20I4 before the Labour Court and the Tribunal dismissed the ID on 
the sole ground of limitation by applying section 2A(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 


9. Subsequently, the Petitioner preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court of Madras 
in W.P.(MD) No.4269 of 20I7 and the Hon’ble High Court vide its order dated .04.207 
under para 8 held as under:- 


“8. The learned counsel for the respondent also relied upon a judgment of this Court in 
W.P. No. 5552 of 20I5 wherein a learned Single Judge of this Court has dismissed a 
similar Writ Petition filed by the workman who challenged the award passed by the 
Labour Court dismissing the claim statement made by the petitioner therein on the ground 
of delay. After referring to the amended provision, this Court has held as follows: 


"The aforesaid provision infers that the workman must raise an industrial dispute before 
the Conciliation Officer and upon expiry of 45 days from the date of filing an 
application before the Conciliation Officer, the workman can move application to the 
Labour Court before the expiry of three years from the date of his dismissal. In any 
event, right conferred under Section 2A of the Act lapse immediately preceding the date 
of expiry of three years of the date of dismissal. Sub-section (3) of Section 2A operates 
independently, despite the continuation of the conciliation proceeding. While such being 
the settled provision, in the case on hand, the petitioner was dismissed from service on 
06.08.20i0. Thereafter, after a lapse of 4 years and 2 months, he filed an application 
under Section 2A(2) of the I.D. Act before the Labour Court only on 3!.0.204. At this 
juncture, the contention of the petitioner is that he was unable to file an application 
before the Labour Court, since his application filed before the Conciliation Officer was 
pending. Such contention of the petitioner cannot stand to legal scrutiny, for, Sub- 
Section 3 of Section 2A of the Act operates independently, despite the continuation of 
the conciliation proceedings. Therefore, he ought to have filed an application before the 
learned Labour Court with three years from the date of dismissal order passed by the 
first respondent Corporation on 06.08.200." 


Accordingly, the Writ Petition was dismissed and the order of the Tribunal was confirmed. 


0. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Petitioner argued that time must be 
counted from the date of failure of conciliation proceedings before the Labour Commissioner. 
This contention of the learned counsel for the Petitioner is against the provisions of section 
2A(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 


ll. Section 2A(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, !947 runs as under:- 


"Section 2A of the principal Act shall be numbered as sub- section (7) thereof and after sub- 
section (/) as so numbered, the following sub-sections shall be inserted, namely: - 


(2) anything Notwithstanding contained in section 70, any such workman as is specified in sub- 
section (3) may, make an application direct to the Labour Court or Tribunal for adjudication of 
the dispute referred to therein after the expiry of forty-five days from the date he has made the

application to the Conciliation Officer of the appropriate Government for conciliation of the 
dispute, and in receipt of such application the Labour Court or Tribunal shall have powers and 
jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the dispute, as if it were a dispute referred to it by the appropriate 
Government in accordance with the provisions of this Act and all the provisions of this Act shall 
apply in relation to such adjudication as they apply in relation to an industrial dispute referred 
to it by the appropriate Government. 


(3) The application referred to in sub-section (2) shall be made to the Labour Court or Tribunal 
before the expiry of three years from the date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or otherwise 
termination of service as specified in sub-section (/). 


2. As per the case of Mr. Prince Packianathan Vs. The General Manager, Tamil Nadu 
Transport Corporation in W.P (MD) No.I5552 of 205 dated 28.08.20I5 passed by the 
Hon'ble High Court of Madras, aforesaid provision infers that the workman must raise an 
industrial dispute before the Conciliation Officer and upon expiry of 45 days from the date of 
filing an application before the Conciliation Officer, the workman can move application to the 
Labour Court before the expiry of three years from the date of his dismissal. In any event, right 
conferred under Section 2A of the Act lapse immediately preceding the date of expiry of three 
years of the date of dismissal. Sub-section (3) of Section 2A operates independently, despite the 
continuation of the conciliation proceeding. 


3. This Tribunal is bound by the above findings of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in the 
case of Prince Packianathan cited supra. The limitation period prescribed under the above 
provision is mandatory and this Tribunal has no discretion to extend the period of limitation. 
This fact is established that the Petitioner after expiry of three years has preferred the claim 
petition before this Tribunal on 2" September, 2022. Therefore, in the light of the above 
reasons, the claim petition filed by the Petitioner is dismissed mere on the ground of being time 
barred in limini.

As per discussion above, the claim petition filed by the Petitioner is barred by limitation and 
the same is dismissed as barred by limitation.
